Byers |ac1_year = 3rd |asst_coach2 = David Moats |ac2_year = 1st |stadium = [[Cassell Coliseum]] |tourney = |tourney_result = }} {{2025–26 ACC men's basketball standings}} The '''2025–26 Virginia Tech Hokies men's basketball team''' represented [[Virginia Tech]] during the [[2025–26 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. The Hokies, led by seventh-year head coach [[Mike Young (basketball)|Mike Young]], played their home games at [[Cassell Coliseum]] in [[Blacksburg, Virginia]], as members of the [[Atlantic Coast Conference]]. The Hokies won their first four games, including an [[Overtime (sports)#Basketball|overtime]] victory over [[2025–26 Providence Friars men's basketball team|Providence]] in the Hall of Fame Tip-Off. They then traveled to [[The Bahamas]] to participate in the [[Battle 4 Atlantis#Men's 2|Battle 4 Atlantis]]. The Hokies won their first game of the tournament by two-points over [[2025–26 Colorado State Rams men's basketball team|Colorado State]]. However they lost in the semifinal game 66–77 against [[2025–26 Saint Mary's Gaels men's basketball team|Saint Mary's]]. The finished in fourth place after losing the third place game against [[2025–26 VCU Rams men's basketball team|VCU]]. They returned to the US mainland and defeated [[2025–26 South Carolina Gamecocks men's basketball team|South Carolina]] in overtime in their [[ACC–SEC Challenge]] game. The team won their last four non-conference games, including an overtime victory against [[2025–26 Elon Phoenix men's basketball team|Elon]] to close out their non-conference schedule. They began ACC play with a triple-overtime thriller against [[Virginia–Virginia Tech men's basketball rivalry|rivals]] and twenty-first ranked [[2025–26 Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball team|Virginia]] 95–85. The team experienced a slight hang over after that game, losing their next two. The Hokies then went 3–2 in their next five games, where they only played one ranked team, twenty-third ranked [[2025–26 Louisville Cardinals men's basketball team|Louisville]], who they lost to by fourteen-points. The team could not build momentum as they went 2–3 over their next fine games. They played two ranked games over the stretch, winning against twentieth-ranked [[2025–26 Clemson Tigers men's basketball team|Clemson]] by ten-points and losing to fourth-ranked [[2025–26 Duke Blue Devils men's basketball team|Duke]] by fourteen-points. The Hokies finished the season on a 2–4 run, where they defeated [[2025–26 Wake Forest Demon Deacons men's basketball team|Wake Forest]] and [[2025–26 Boston College Eagles men's basketball team|Boston College]]. They lost to eighteenth-ranked [[2025–26 North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball team|North Carolina]] and they closed the season with a loss in their rivalry re-match against thirteenth-ranked Virginia. The Hokies finished the season 19–13 and 8–10 in [[2025–26 Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball season|ACC play]] to finish in a tie for eleventh place. As the twevlfth-seed in the [[2026 ACC men's basketball tournament|2026 ACC tournament]] they faced thirteenth-seed Wake Forest for the third time in the season. After splitting the regular season series, the Hokies lost in the tournament, 89–95, in overtime. Following the loss, the team announced that they preemptively declined a bid to participate in the [[2026 National Invitation Tournament|NIT]], citing team injuries, but declared they would accept a bid to the [[2026 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]].{{cite web |last1=Caudell |first1=Jackson |title=Virginia Tech Announces They Will Not Participate In This Year's NIT Tournament |url=https://www.si.com/college/virginiatech/basketball/virginia-tech-announces-they-will-not-participate-in-this-year-s-nit-tournament-01kkm3atgnfb |website=Sports Illustrated |access-date=March 13, 2026 |date=March 13, 2026}} Days later, they were not invited to the NCAA tournament, bringing their season to a close. ==Previous season== {{main|2024–25 Virginia Tech Hokies men's basketball team}} The Hokies finished the [[2024–25 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|season]] 13–18 and 8–12 in [[2024–25 Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball season|ACC play]] to finish in a five-way tie for ninth place. As the tenth seed in the [[2025 ACC men's basketball tournament|2025 ACC tournament]] they faced fifteenth seed California in the First Round. Virginia Tech couldn't repeat their regular season win and were defeated 82–73 in double-overtime. They were not invited to the [[2025 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] or the [[2025 National Invitation Tournament|NIT]]. ==Offseason== ===Departures=== {| class="wikitable
